title: Refactor multi-language SDK deps, streamline API surface, and deprecate legacy client params
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Coordinate a synchronized dependency bump across Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs to remove legacy compatibility shims and deprecate the old client-side request parameter surface used by <completion_params>. The goal is to reduce maintenance cost, improve request path performance, and remove redundant translation layers between client libs and the runtime. This work touches client transports, generator convenience helpers, and the backwards-compat layer that maps legacy param names to the canonical API.
acceptance_criteria: All three language SDKs (python/js/go) upgrade dependency set to approved matrix: httpx>=0.25, requests>=2.31, node-fetch>=3.3 or axios 1.5+, go-http v1.12+ and proto definitions regenerated

Legacy request param names (eg. 'completion', 'response_format', 'use_legacy_cache') are removed from public client surface or routed through a documented compatibility shim behind a deprecation warning header
Compatibility telemetry emits counts for legacy param usage and appears on the SDK Hygiene dashboard
No regressions in CI for core e2e tests and we have new unit tests asserting deprecation warning headers and mapping behavior
Migration guide published and in the SDK docs with code examples for Python/JS/Go
implementation_notes: Python: update pyproject to pin httpx 0.25+, remove old 'CompatClient' wrapper, add runtime deprecation header middleware. Generate new client models from updated proto and bump version to 1.10.0
JS: consolidate fetch/axios adapters into a single transport abstraction; remove legacy 'response_format' alias and surface deprecation console.warn + server-side header when used
Go: bump go.mod to use internal transport v2, regenerate protobuf bindings, remove shim in top-level client constructor
Add integration test harness that exercises legacy-to-canonical param translation and validates deprecation headers
Coordinate with runtime team to accept both old and new param names for two release cycles; runtime changes in runtime-1.18 will add a warning header when legacy names are used
risks: Some large customers may still be using legacy params in production; need to quantify via telemetry before hard-removal
Dependency upgrades could trigger transitive breakages in downstream consumers (esp. Node bundlers and Go module versions)
Regressions in streaming response code paths if transport adapter changes are not thoroughly tested
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Publish JS/py/go packages with deprecation shims enabled and telemetry for 1 week to internal customers and opt-in enterprise tenants
Phase 2 (Public Warning): Promote packages to stable, push migration docs and automatic deprecation notices in SDK changelog and Console billing/usage email to active API keys
Phase 3 (Grace Period): After 8 weeks, coordinate runtime-side enforcement window where legacy params will return warnings with timelines
Phase 4 (Removal): After 16 weeks and customer outreach, perform breaking removal in SDKs and runtime; attach migration playbook for customers needing assistance
